## Root cause

`docs/.vitepress/config.ts` set `pageData.frontmatter.sidebar = <items>` per page (via `transformPageData`) to avoid embedding the full API tree in the global theme config. But VitePress's default theme (`useLayout`) only reads `frontmatter.sidebar` as a boolean gate (`sidebar: false` hides it) — the actual sidebar content always comes from `theme.value.sidebar`, i.e. `themeConfig.sidebar`, resolved per-route via `getSidebar()`. Since the locale `themeConfig.sidebar` only had a `[locale.guidePrefix]` key and no entry for `/api/`, every API page resolved to an empty sidebar and rendered none — while `/guide/*` kept working because it matched the one key that *was* present.

## Fix

Merged the already-computed, per-route-partitioned `apiSidebarRoutesByLocale[localeKey]` map into each locale's `themeConfig.sidebar` object (VitePress's real multi-path sidebar mechanism) instead of injecting into frontmatter, and removed the now-dead `apiSidebarFor`/`pagePath` helpers and the frontmatter injection in `transformPageData`. Verified in the browser that `/api/`, `/api/css/`, and `/guide/getting-started` all render their sidebars correctly.
